div.head: AGu 3
div.ab: ⁊ gif man cyninges ðegn beteo manslihtes, gif he hine ladian dyrre, do he þæt mid XII cininges ðegnum; gif ma ðone man betyhð, ðe bið læssa maga ðone se cyninges ðegn, ladige he hine mid XI his gelicena ⁊ mid anum cyninges ðægne — ⁊ swa ægehwilcre spræce ðe mare sy ðone IIII mancussas —; ⁊ gyf he ne dyrre, gylde hit ðrygylde, swa hit man gewyrðe.
⁊ gyf man cynges ðegen beteo manslihtas, ⁊ he hine ladian durre, do hé þæt mid XII cynges þegnas; ⁊ gyf mon ðone man betyhð, þe bið læssa maga, ladie híne XI his gelicena ⁊ anum cýninges ðegene.

Si thainus regis accusetur de homicidio, si se purgare uelit, faciat hoc cum XII thainis regis; si thainus accusetur, qui minus possit quam thainus regis, adlegiet se cum XI parium suorum et cum uno regis thaino — et sic in omni causa que maior sit quam IIII mance —; et si non audeat, soluat illam tripliciter, sicut adpretiabitur.

[Be ðegnum ðe betogene synd.] ⁊ gif man cyninges ðegn beteo manslihtes, gif he hine ladian dyrre, do he ðæt mid XII cininges ðegnum; gif mon ðone man betyhð, ðe bið læssa maga ðone se cyninges ðegn, ladige he hine mid XI his gelicena ⁊ mid anum cyninges ðægne—⁊ swa ægehwilcre spræce ðe mare sy ðone IIII mancussas—; ⁊ gyf he ne dyrre, gylde hit ðrygylde, swa hit man gewyrðe.

(Über Thegnas, welche verklagt werden. Ld) Und wenn man einen Königsthegn des Todtschlags anklagt, wenn (und Ld) er sich rein zu schwören wagt, thu’ er das mit 12 Königsthegnas; (und B2) wenn man einen solchen Mann (Thegn Ld Quadr.) anklagt, welcher weniger vermögend als der Königsthegn ist, reinige er sich mit 11 seines Gleichen und mit Einem Königsthegn — und so bei jeder Klage, die mehr beträgt als 4 Mancussen —; und wenn jener [Verklagte diese Reinigung] nicht wagt, so vergelte er das [Eingeklagte] mit dreifachem Entgelt, je wie man es [gerichtlich] schätzt.

(Of thegns who are accused. Ld) And if a king’s thegn is accused of manslaughter, if (and Ld) he dares to clear himself by oath, let him do so with 12 king’s thegns; (and B2) if such a man (thegn Ld Quadr.) is accused who is of less standing than the king’s thegn, let him clear himself with 11 of his equals and with one king’s thegn — and so in every suit which amounts to more than 4 mancuses —; and if that [accused man] does not dare [this exculpation], let him pay for [what is claimed] with threefold payment, as it is [judicially] valued.

If anyone accuses a king's thegn of homicide, if he dares to clear himself, he shall do so with [the oaths of] twelve king's thegns. If anyone accuses a man who belongs to a lower order than that of king's thegn, he shall clear himself with [the oaths of] eleven of his equals and one king's thegn. And this law shall apply to every suit which involves an amount greater than 4 mancuses. And if he [the accused] dare not [attempt to clear himself], he shall pay [as compensation] three times the amount at which the stolen property is valued.

And if anyone accuses a king’s thegn of manslaughter, if he dares to clear himself by oath, he is to do it with 12 king’s thegns; if anyone accuses a man who is less powerful then a king’s thegn, he is to clear himself with 12 of his equals and with one king’s thegn—and so in every suit which involves more than four mancuses—and if he dare not [clear himself], he is to pay three-fold compensation, according as it is valued.

Maurer bevorzugt die Lesart ‘Mann’ Adel 174; Kr. Übsch. II 410; die zahlreichste Klasse, die der Ceorlas, wäre ja sonst unerwähnt. — Die Lesart lq's aber erklärt sich durch den Gebrauch des Wortes thegn (s. d. Gl 8) für jeden Vollfreien oder durch Erinnerung an den læsseþegn (s. Wb) oder durch Benutzung von II Cn 71, 5, wo ein Thegn læsse maga ist als der Königsthegn

Maurer prefers the reading ‘man’, Adel 174; Kr. Übsch. II 410; for otherwise the most numerous class, that of the ceorlas, would go unmentioned. — The reading of lq, however, is explained by the use of the word thegn (see that word in Gl 8) for every fully free man, or by recollection of the læsseþegn (see Wb), or by use of II Cn 71, 5, where a thegn is læsse maga than the king's thegn
Adverb; s. II Atr 9; ‘geringeren Standes’ ist nicht wörtlich; maga ist Adjektiv
Adverb; see II Atr 9; ‘of lesser rank’ is not literal; maga is an adjective
Vgl. Gl Standesgenossen 5. Schon Ine misstraut dem bloss bäuerlichen Eide
Cf. Gl Standesgenossen 5. Ine already distrusts the oath of a mere peasant

¹/₂ £; s. Gl Mancus 5. Grosser, von Todesstrafe bedrohter Diebstahl (s. d. Gl 9c) begann bei weit geringerer Summe. Ein Vergleich mit dem bei Totschlag an einem Freien mindestens auf dem Spiele stehenden Wergeld von 200 Schilling = 33¹/₃ Mancus kommt also nicht in Frage. — Über den Beweis in dem sicher weit häufigeren Prozess um geringere Summen, z. B. ein Rind, erfahren wir nichts

¹/₂ £; see Gl Mancus 5. Grand larceny, punishable by death (see that word in Gl 9c), began at a far lower sum. A comparison with the wergild of 200 shillings = 33¹/₃ mancuses which is at stake, at the least, in the killing of a freeman is therefore out of the question. — About the proof in the certainly far more frequent suits over lesser sums, e.g. an ox, we learn nothing

Adverb; Wülfing Syntax I 266: ‘dreifach’. So auch III Atr 4. — Steenstrup sieht hierin die Busse (s. d. Gl 18) der Denalagu; allein derselbe Satz herrscht auch in Kent. — Laut letzter 4 Worte bezieht sich dies, wie schon Q verstand, nur auf Vermögensklage, nicht (wie genau logische Interpretation und der Gegensatz dieses gif he ne dyrre zu obigem gif he hine ladian dyrre erfordern) auch auf Wergeld; dieses ist, wenn Totschläger erst im Klagewege zu Zahlung gezwungen werden muss, nicht etwa zu verdreifachen. — Vgl. Gl Taxe 1

Adverb; Wülfing Syntax I 266: ‘threefold’. So also III Atr 4. — Steenstrup sees in this the compensation (see that word in Gl 18) of the Danelaw; but the same rule also prevails in Kent. — According to the last 4 words this refers, as Q already understood, only to a claim for property, and not also to wergild (as a strictly logical interpretation and the contrast between this gif he ne dyrre and the gif he hine ladian dyrre above would require); wergild is not, say, to be tripled when a slayer must first be compelled to pay by legal action. — Cf. Gl Taxe 1
The oath of a king’s thegn was equal to that of 12 commoners (see Chadwick, op. cit. p. 134 ff.).

The mancus was a gold coin weighing about 70 grains. It contained 30 pence. The earliest belongs to the reign of Offa and in addition to the legend Offa Rex it bears a long Arabic inscription, copied from a Mohammedan coin. The name is Arabic in origin, and is derived from man-kush, lit. ‘stamped’ (cf. Chadwick, op. cit. p. 10 ff.).
